question: Čokoláda, ktorú ste nechali v horúcom aute, po vychladnutí niekedy na povrchu zbelie. Nie je to pleseň. Čo je teda ten biely povlak?
source_excerpt: Fat bloom occurs when the cocoa butter in chocolate melts, it separates from the cocoa solids and rises to the surface

extra.why_interesting: Nearly everyone has found a whitened chocolate bar and assumed it was mouldy or spoiled. The surprise is that the white layer is the chocolate's own fat, which melted and set again on the surface. Players can reason toward the answer from 'heat melts fat'.
extra.verification_notes: Heat-induced bloom is fat bloom, where cocoa butter melts, rises to the surface and recrystallises as a white coating (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocolate_bloom).

explanation: Teplo roztopí kakaové maslo, ktoré vystúpi na povrch a pri chladnutí znova stuhne do bielych kryštálikov. Čokoláda je úplne v poriadku, len sa jej trochu pokazil vzhľad.

question: Názov čokolády Milka vznikol spojením dvoch nemeckých slov, ktoré označujú jej hlavné suroviny. Ktoré sú to suroviny?
source_excerpt: The name Milka is a portmanteau of the German words for milk (Milch) and cocoa (Kakao).

extra.why_interesting: Milka is in every Slovak shop and the purple cow is familiar, but few people have stopped to think about the name. Once the question gives the clue that it combines two ingredients, players can work it out themselves and get a satisfying 'of course!' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Milka's name is widely documented as a blend of German 'Milch' and 'Kakao' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milka).

explanation: Milka vznikla z nemeckých slov „Milch“, čiže mlieko, a „Kakao“. Preto má vo svojom znaku kravičku, a nie kakaovník.
